title: Why the array index is a bad key

slides.say: Using the array index as a key is tempting. It often leads to subtle and confusing bugs.
This silences the warning. In fact, if you give no key at all, React uses the index anyway.

slides.text: Insert, delete or reorder an item, and the indexes move. Key 0 is now a different item.
slides.say: But when an item is inserted, deleted, or the list is reordered, the indexes shift. Key zero now points at a different item, so React can mix up their state.

slides.text: Use a stable ID from the data.
slides.say: The fix: use a stable ID that belongs to the data itself. It stays with the item wherever it moves.
